Hey Portland network, does anyone know of a venue that could host about 60 people for a creative-tech meetup?

Trying to get something going where local folks can see cool work and actually meet each other in person. Nothing corporate — just power and some open floor.

Hit me up if you know a spot, or just drop a comment. 👇

Toured Rose City Machine Co. out in NE Portland yesterday and I'm still thinking about it.

Dave Kessler and his partner Mia Torres run a proper fab shop — CNC, laser cutting, a woodshop in the back — and they rent out machine time to local artists for basically the cost of material. No corporate minimums, no three-week onboarding, just book a slot and go.

This is exactly the kind of thing that makes a city's creative scene actually work, and I think what they're building is cool.

Check it out if you're anywhere near Portland. 👏

Got some Bracket Bear news coming next week, folks. Sitting on this is rough...

#bracketbear2026

I think AI coding agents are less about writing code faster and more about how small teams trust each other.

Why?

Because when one dev with Cursor or Claude Code can ship what used to take a team of four, the bottleneck stops being output. It becomes: do you trust the person driving the agent to make good calls without someone checking every line?

I've watched this happen firsthand this year — smaller teams shipping bigger scopes, and the ones doing it well are the ones that already had high trust before the tools showed up.

Maybe the real skill in 2026 isn't prompting. It's building a team you don't have to babysit.

Heard that my buddy Alex Chen and the Lightwell crew just landed a massive install downtown.

So freaking happy for them. 🤘
